The roll burns: nobody can prove what anyone owes; the gang scatters on the shore. Three places within a day change: the camp (the cutting withdrawn, the clutch grey), the barge (the crew parent off), the paddies behind the camp (the families on the shore).

The Owing roll (labour-and-bondage §2): the debt is months owed, with months added for food; the holder is a Lilmoth debt-labour broker who bought the gang's months from earlier holders (drift 2, transferable) and hires it to Hereguard Plantation; the overseer reads the roll; the exit in law is working the months off, and in practice the food months outrun the work, so the gang families are born into it. The bound want to be home under their own Hist, and have the right to refuse help: the washed-out woman will not leave the gang while her daughter owes.
none the player can stop: the cell cuts the roots at dusk as the player is at the fire; the player can only choose which one of the two witnesses lives

Two of the gang are visibly washed out from years away from their Hist, and their cutting is cut; the player's own line is blank, so no amount of work can pay it down. Whoever the player does not reach in the burning camp dies, and the gang families lose their clutch.
The cutting's withdrawal: the light in the cutting goes out and the sap stops, in front of the gang families, with the harvest at its roots as the officiant and the severed clutch as the sign.
the voice is Cuts-the-Old-Knot's, the cell's leader, unnamed to the player until much later (§18d)
